book_review.problem: The space-like case is proved in three explicit stages. The time-like case is dismissed with 'in the same way', although its boost sets a different stage (cosh theta = |tau|, not |sigma|) and the roles of the two rotation stages are exchanged.

book_review.fix: Write the three stages. (1) A boost in the plane (x4, x8) carries e_{x4} to |tau| e_{x4} + |sigma| e_{x8}: by (E), sinh theta = ±|sigma| with the sign fixed by (E), so cosh theta = sqrt(1 + |sigma|^2) = |tau|. (2) Rotations in (x8, x1), (x8, x2), (x8, x3) turn e_{x8} into sigma/|sigma| without touching x4. (3) Rotations in (x4, x5), (x4, x6), (x4, x7) turn e_{x4} into tau/|tau|, giving sigma + tau = v. book_review.problem: Two steps of the Wick-theorem proof are skipped. First, the four-operator formula is said to transform 'in the same way, factor by factor', with no line written. Second, Wick's theorem for a thermal ensemble is asserted because the occupations are independent, 'which is all the proof needs'. The thermal four-operator expectation is never derived, and Section 13.26 proves only the independence.
book_review.evidence: Quoted: 'which is the matrix element of the same rho between the new orbitals; the four-operator formula transforms in the same way, factor by factor. ... It also holds, with occupations f_a between 0 and 1 ..., for a thermal ensemble ... (Section 13.26 shows that the occupations of different orbitals are then independent, which is all the proof needs).' grep shows Section 13.26 (lines 2972-2984) derives independent Fermi-Dirac occupations but no <a+_p a+_q a_s a_r> formula.
book_review.fix: Insert the line <a'+_p a'+_q a'_s a'_r> = sum_{k,l,m,n} U_kp U_lq U*_ms U*_nr <a+_k a+_l a_m a_n> = sum U_kp U_lq U*_ms U*_nr (rho_nk rho_ml - rho_mk rho_nl) = rho'_rp rho'_sq - rho'_sp rho'_rq, with rho' = U^dagger rho U. Give the rule: linearity, then the determinant formula, then regroup the sums into matrix products. For the thermal case, add: in the eigen-orbitals of the ensemble, <a+_p a_q> = delta_pq f_p, because states with different occupations are orthogonal. For p != q, <n_p n_q> = f_p f_q by independence. So <a+_p a+_q a_s a_r> = f_p f_q (delta_pr delta_qs - delta_ps delta_qr) = rho_rp rho_sq - rho_sp rho_rq with rho = diag(f), and the basis change above carries this to every basis.

book_review.location: Section 12.6, line 292 ('The extra-time component is found in the same way')
book_review.problem: The collected-sum line is skipped for G^{x5}_{x5}, although it is written out for G^{x1}_{x1}. Only the pair counts and the final result are given.
book_review.evidence: Quoted: 'The extra-time component is found in the same way (three 3-space pairs, one extra-time pair, six mixed pairs, three space-time pairs, two extra-time-time pairs, five with x_8): sum = 3(a_4')^2 - 15H^2 + a_4''.' I checked it from the 12.5 table: (3+1-6+3+2)(a4')^2 + (-3-1-6-5)H^2 + (3-2)a4'' = 3(a4')^2 - 15H^2 + a4''. The result is correct; only the line is missing.
book_review.fix: Insert the display: sum = (3 + 1 - 6 + 3 + 2)(a_4')^2 + (-3 - 1 - 6 - 5)H^2 + (3 - 2)a_4'' = 3(a_4')^2 - 15H^2 + a_4''. Rule: the table row by row (the x4x8 pair contributes 0); collect the (a_4')^2, H^2 and a_4'' terms. Replace 'is found in the same way' with 'uses the pairs without x_5'.
